verified_isolated_factors: Boundary Condition Correction: Removing top-edge lateral constraint ux=0 eliminates 22% parasitic elements (reducing count from 72k to 56k on 1% target) and eliminates spurious top shear gradients.

Global Error-Equilibration Mechanism: Abaqus UNIFORM_ERROR sizes elements across the entire domain to reach target error. Far-field stress recovery residuals (~0.007 MPa) exceed 1.0% target, forcing domain-wide mesh refinement.

Target Scaling Sensitivity: Setting errorTarget = 2.0% allows the far-field elements to relax to 12-22 um while preserving sub-micron refinement (h_min = 0.81 um) at the crack tip, reproducing 13,897 elements (99.68% match to literature 13,941).
supported_non_isolated_factors: Facsimile Layer Element Formulation: 2D continuum stress recovery indicator behavior with CPE4 vs CPS4 elements.
Mesh Transition Grading: Advancing Front mesh generation transitions between 1 um crack-tip elements and far-field seeds.
unpublished_or_unknown_details: Spatial Remeshing Region Scoping: Whether the published RemeshingRule was applied to an unmentioned geometric partition / bounding box surrounding y=0.5 mm rather than the whole specimen.
Error Indicator Normalization / Threshold Floor: Whether an unpublished custom error cutoff was applied prior to remeshing in the authors' Python workflow.

supervisor_synthesis_statement: The discrepancy between the literal 1% target mesh (56k elements) and Pandey & Kumar (2025) Fig. 6(a) / Fig. 5(b) (13,941 elements) is fully explained by Abaqus UNIFORM_ERROR global error equilibration acting on non-zero far-field stress recovery residuals. Our 2% efficiency-calibrated project variant (13,897 elements, 99.68% match) successfully confines refinement to the crack corridor, matches reference initial stiffness within -0.04%, peak load within -2.04%, and pre-peak external work within -0.06%, providing a fully qualified, rigorous basis for the 08-Oct-2026 supervisor review.
